editorial:
Imagine being seventeen years old and suddenly ripped away from your books and friends to fight in a war you do not understand. That is exactly what happens to Werner and Gilbert. At first, they are just kids, but the army changes them in very different ways. Gilbert drinks the propaganda and becomes a true believer in the cause, while Werner starts to see the horror and the waste of life around him. It is a heavy story, but it feels real because it focuses on the friendship between two boys who are being pushed apart by hate and politics.

The acting is great because you can really see the change in Werner's eyes as he loses his innocence. The movie moves at a steady pace, though some parts feel a bit slow if you are looking for big explosions. It is more about the feelings and the moral struggle than the fighting. If you enjoy historical stories that make you think, you should definitely check this out. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The story ends on a sad note. Werner tries to stay human in a cruel system, but he eventually faces the harsh reality of the war. He realizes that the ideology he was taught is a lie. The final scenes show the total collapse of their world. While Gilbert stays blinded by his loyalty, Werner ends up broken, showing that the war destroys everyone, regardless of which side they are on.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful stories about friendship and history.
